column1: # Name-table language IDs: (platform, langID) → language, for the localized
# metadata shown in the Font Overview dialog.
# Authoritative sources (both are the references the OpenType 'name' table
# spec itself points to):
#   platform 1 (Macintosh): Apple TrueType Reference Manual — 'name' table,
#     "The language identifier (Macintosh platform)",
#     https://developer.apple.com/fonts/TrueType-Reference-Manual/RM06/Chap6name.html
#   platform 3 (Windows):   [MS-LCID] Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID)
#     Reference (Microsoft Open Specifications),
#     https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-lcid/
#     — as referenced by the OpenType 'name' table spec,
#     https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/name
# lang_id is the numeric language ID used in OpenType name records (given in
# hex; the loader accepts 0x… or decimal).  For Windows this is the low 16
# bits of the LCID.
# name    = the language name exactly as published by the source above.
# display = canonical short label used for grouping/display in the UI.
#           Sublanguage variants of one language collapse onto the same
#           display label (e.g. US/UK/AU English → "English"; zh-Hant /
#           zh-Hans → "Chinese (Traditional)" / "Chinese (Simplified)") so a
#           font that carries several sublanguage records still shows one
#           block per language.
# Columns: platform<TAB>lang_id<TAB>name<TAB>display
# platform 3 (Windows) — language IDs from [MS-LCID] (the low 16 bits of the
# LCID, as used in OpenType name records).
